description: This topic covers the meaning, conditions, main rites, and spiritual and social significance of Hajj and Umrah, and the difference between them.

mcq.questionText: Which pillar of Islam is the pilgrimage to Makkah?
mcq.explanation: Hajj is the fifth pillar of Islam, after the testimony of faith, prayer, zakat and fasting.

mcq.questionText: How many times in a lifetime is Hajj obligatory upon a Muslim who is able?
mcq.explanation: Hajj is obligatory once in a lifetime for a Muslim who meets the conditions; any additional Hajj is voluntary.

mcq.questionText: What is the special state of sacredness that a pilgrim enters before performing Hajj or Umrah called?
mcq.explanation: Ihram is the sacred state, marked by special clothing and intention, that a pilgrim enters before the rites begin.

mcq.questionText: Walking around the Ka'bah seven times during the pilgrimage is known as:
mcq.explanation: Tawaf is the act of circling the Ka'bah seven times in worship of Allah.

mcq.questionText: The act of walking briskly between the hills of Safa and Marwah is called:
mcq.explanation: Sa'i is the walking between Safa and Marwah, recalling the search for water by Hajar, the wife of Prophet Ibrahim.

mcq.questionText: Standing at the plain of Arafah on the ninth day of Dhul-Hijjah is considered:

options.text: The most essential rite of Hajj

mcq.explanation: Standing at Arafah (wuquf) is the central rite of Hajj; without it the Hajj is not valid.

mcq.questionText: In which Islamic month is Hajj performed?
mcq.explanation: Hajj is performed during the month of Dhul-Hijjah, the twelfth month of the Islamic calendar.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a main difference between Hajj and Umrah?

options.text: Umrah includes standing at Arafah but Hajj does not
Hajj has a fixed time of year while Umrah can be done at any time
Umrah is one of the five pillars while Hajj is not

mcq.explanation: Hajj is performed only during the days of Dhul-Hijjah, whereas Umrah may be performed at any time of the year.

mcq.questionText: Umrah is sometimes called by which of these names?
mcq.explanation: Umrah is known as the lesser pilgrimage because it has fewer rites than Hajj and is not bound to a fixed time.

mcq.questionText: Which condition must be met for Hajj to become obligatory on a Muslim?
mcq.explanation: Hajj is obligatory only on a Muslim who has the financial means and physical ability to undertake the journey safely.

mcq.questionText: Which group of people is NOT required to perform Hajj?

options.text: Adult, sane Muslims who are able
Those who lack the means and ability
Free Muslims who can afford the journey

mcq.explanation: Hajj is not obligatory on a person who does not have the financial or physical ability to perform it.

mcq.questionText: The pilgrims' chant proclaiming response to Allah's call during Hajj is known as the:
mcq.explanation: The Talbiyah is the call recited by pilgrims expressing their response and devotion to Allah during Hajj and Umrah.

mcq.questionText: What does the gathering of millions of pilgrims from different nations during Hajj demonstrate?

options.text: The superiority of one race over others
The unity and equality of the Muslim Ummah
That only Arabs may perform Hajj
That wealth determines a pilgrim's status

mcq.explanation: Pilgrims of all races and nations wearing simple ihram together show the unity, brotherhood and equality of Muslims.

mcq.questionText: Which rite is performed during both Hajj and Umrah?
mcq.explanation: Tawaf around the Ka'bah is a shared rite of both Hajj and Umrah, while standing at Arafah belongs to Hajj alone.

mcq.questionText: The historical roots of the Hajj rites are closely connected to which prophet and his family?
mcq.explanation: Many rites of Hajj, such as Sa'i and the building of the Ka'bah, are linked to Prophet Ibrahim and his family.

fib.questionText: Hajj is the _____ pillar of Islam.
fib.explanation: Hajj completes the five pillars of Islam.

fib.questionText: The sacred state a pilgrim enters before the rites of Hajj is called _____.
fib.explanation: Ihram involves a special intention and prescribed dress.

fib.questionText: Circling the Ka'bah seven times is known as _____.
fib.explanation: Tawaf is performed around the Ka'bah in worship of Allah.

fib.questionText: Walking between the hills of Safa and Marwah is called _____.
fib.explanation: Sa'i recalls Hajar's search for water for her son Isma'il.

fib.questionText: The most essential rite of Hajj is the standing at _____.
fib.explanation: Without standing at Arafah on the ninth of Dhul-Hijjah, the Hajj is invalid.

fib.questionText: Hajj is performed in the month of _____.
fib.explanation: Dhul-Hijjah is the twelfth month of the Islamic calendar.

fib.questionText: Umrah is also known as the _____ pilgrimage because it has fewer rites than Hajj.
fib.explanation: Umrah is called the lesser or minor pilgrimage and can be done at any time.

fib.questionText: Hajj becomes obligatory only on a Muslim who is _____ to perform it.
fib.explanation: Ability refers to financial means and physical health for the journey.

fib.questionText: The chant by which pilgrims respond to Allah's call during Hajj is the _____.
fib.explanation: The Talbiyah expresses the pilgrim's devotion and response to Allah.

fib.questionText: The Ka'bah is located in the city of _____.
fib.explanation: Makkah is the holy city to which Muslims travel to perform Hajj and Umrah.

tf.questionText: Hajj is obligatory on every Muslim once in a lifetime if they are able.
tf.explanation: Hajj is required once in a lifetime for those who have the means and ability.

tf.questionText: Umrah can only be performed during the month of Dhul-Hijjah.
tf.explanation: Unlike Hajj, Umrah may be performed at any time of the year.

tf.questionText: Ihram is a state of sacredness that includes special intention and dress.
tf.explanation: Pilgrims enter ihram before beginning the rites of Hajj or Umrah.

tf.questionText: Standing at Arafah is part of Umrah.
tf.explanation: Standing at Arafah is a rite of Hajj only, not of Umrah.

tf.questionText: Tawaf means walking around the Ka'bah seven times.
tf.explanation: Tawaf is the circling of the Ka'bah seven times in worship.

tf.questionText: Hajj is not obligatory on a person who lacks the financial and physical means.
tf.explanation: Ability is a condition for Hajj to become obligatory.

tf.questionText: During Hajj, pilgrims of all nations and races wear similar simple garments.
tf.explanation: The simple ihram dress symbolises equality and unity among Muslims.

tf.questionText: Sa'i is performed between the hills of Safa and Marwah.
tf.explanation: Sa'i is the walking between Safa and Marwah during the pilgrimage.

tf.questionText: Umrah includes more rites than Hajj.
tf.explanation: Umrah has fewer rites than Hajj, which is why it is called the lesser pilgrimage.

tf.questionText: Hajj has both spiritual and social significance for Muslims.
tf.explanation: Hajj brings spiritual purification and strengthens social unity and brotherhood.

summary.correctAnswer: Hajj is the pilgrimage to the Ka'bah in Makkah performed at a fixed time.
summary.explanation: It is the fifth pillar of Islam.

summary.correctAnswer: An adult, sane Muslim who is financially and physically able.
summary.explanation: Ability and soundness of mind and body are conditions.

summary.correctAnswer: The sacred state of intention and dress entered before the rites.
summary.explanation: It marks the start of Hajj or Umrah.

summary.correctAnswer: Walking around the Ka'bah seven times in worship.
summary.explanation: A shared rite of Hajj and Umrah.

summary.correctAnswer: Walking between the hills of Safa and Marwah.
summary.explanation: It recalls Hajar's search for water.

summary.correctAnswer: Standing at the plain of Arafah on the ninth of Dhul-Hijjah.
Hajj has a fixed time and more rites; Umrah is shorter and any time.
It purifies the soul, increases taqwa and seeks forgiveness from Allah.
It unites Muslims of all nations and teaches equality and brotherhood.
summary.explanation: All pilgrims wear the same simple dress.

summary.questionText: Unity of the Ummah at Hajj
summary.correctAnswer: Millions gather as one community worshipping one Allah.
summary.explanation: It shows the global brotherhood of Islam.

hoq.questionText: A wealthy but seriously ill Muslim who cannot travel safely wishes to know his duty regarding Hajj. What is the correct position?

options.text: Hajj remains obligatory and he must travel immediately
Hajj is not currently obligatory because physical ability is a condition
He must perform Umrah instead as a replacement for Hajj
He is forever exempt and the duty never applies to him

hoq.explanation: Physical ability is a condition for Hajj; while genuinely unable, the obligation does not apply to him at that time.

hoq.questionText: Why is the simple, identical ihram clothing worn by all pilgrims considered especially meaningful for the Ummah?

options.text: It is cheaper than ordinary clothing
It removes signs of wealth and rank, showing equality before Allah
It identifies which country each pilgrim comes from
It is required only for leaders of the pilgrimage

hoq.explanation: By dressing alike, rich and poor stand equal, demonstrating that all people are equal in the sight of Allah.

hoq.questionText: A student says, 'Performing Umrah during the year fulfils the obligation of Hajj.' How should this statement be judged?

options.text: Correct, because both are pilgrimages to Makkah
Correct, because Umrah includes standing at Arafah
Incorrect, because Hajj and Umrah are distinct and Umrah does not replace Hajj
Incorrect, because Umrah is forbidden outside Dhul-Hijjah

hoq.explanation: Umrah is a separate, lesser pilgrimage and does not fulfil the obligation of Hajj, which has its own time and rites.
